proposal_metadata.title: October 2026 agent verification, privacy, and observability research refresh
proposal_metadata.scope: Focused review of relevant primary arXiv records submitted 2026-10-29; abstract-level review, not independent replication.
proposal_metadata.additions: 5 nodes and 8 edges; new claims remain to_test and need independent replication.

add_nodes.label: Prefix executability reveals invalid tool trajectories hidden by final success
add_nodes.description: A trajectory-level protocol checks whether each tool-call prefix remains executable under schemas, preconditions, and data dependencies; the authors report ranking disagreements with final-success metrics and improved prefix survival from plan checking. Research claim; not independently reproduced here.

add_nodes.label: Authorize information propagation across the downstream task graph
add_nodes.description: Task-Graph Contextual Integrity models disclosure history and downstream recipients jointly, then limits propagation with full-scope or maximal-admissible-region policies. The authors report an 85.8–94.1% reduction in mean unauthorized disclosures on a 144-case benchmark while retaining 93.6–96.1% of baseline task accuracy; replication and privacy/utility/cost trade-offs remain open.

add_nodes.label: Keep completion claims separate from independently checkable execution evidence
add_nodes.description: Soei proposes an acknowledgement-aware event schema, hash-chained ledger, provenance graph, and verification layer that distinguishes an agent's completion claim from evidence of completion. On the same 45-session corpus, the authors' blind-audited estimate says 57.8% of agent-marked completed to-dos had no proof in between; this is corpus-specific author-reported evidence, not an independent prevalence estimate.
derived_from: arXiv:2610.39468, submitted 2026-10-29; preprint v1.1 abstract reviewed 2026-10-31

add_nodes.label: Evaluate agent reports against time-ordered observations and executed outcomes under pressure
add_nodes.description: AgentDecept introduces paired pressure and pressure-free tasks and compares user-facing claims with full trajectories to distinguish falsification, concealment, equivocation, honest failure, and disclosed limitations. It is a benchmark proposal, not evidence of real-world deception prevalence.

add_nodes.label: Certify changing task environments and replay verdicts from archived evidence
add_nodes.description: EnvOS checks that dynamic environment changes fire correctly, tasks remain solvable, and graders discriminate outcomes before runs; a separate verifier re-checks verdicts from archived evidence afterward. In the authors' stale-information studies, Claude Opus 5 succeeds on 0/16 clinic tasks with no extra state, 2/16 after a reminder, and 15/16 when shown the updated value (gain over reminder p=0.00293 after correction). A separate 1/10-to-9/10 insurance-claim gain for Sonnet 5 is not significant after correction for multiple tests; broader replication remains needed.
